journal_lines: Roots in the water first, then down to the mud.
A frog on the root arch I was about to step over. Stepped around it.
The aerial roots hang like curtains. Patience required.
Dense, uneven wood. A life lived half in water.
Stood in mud past the second knuckle for an hour. The mud did not seem to mind.
A heron watched from a snag, very still. Then suddenly elsewhere.
The water held the shape of the roots even after I had passed.
Tangled roots like a question nobody had answered in centuries.
Smelled like salt and patience. Two old smells.
Found a turtle on a low root, sunning. Worked the far side of the grove instead.
